6900-rudin-a-novel.description: A book by Ivan Turgenev. nto mould, he stands even higher than as a pure creator. Tolstoi is more plastical, and certainly as deep and original and rich in creative power as Turgenev, and Dostoevsky is more intense, fervid, and dramatic.

71707-the-africanders.title: In South Africa
71707-the-africanders.creator: Le Roy Hooker,
71707-the-africanders.description: A book by Le Roy Hooker,. This is the history, briefly told, of the great Dutch-English feud in South Africa, up to the beginning of the Africanders’ second war of independence with Great Britain, which opened on the 11th of October, 1899.

arxiv-1612-08388.title: Clustering Algorithms: A Comparative Approach
arxiv-1612-08388.creator: Mayra Z. Rodriguez 1, Cesar H. Comin 2, Dalcimar Casanova 3, Odemir M. Bruno 2, Diego R. Amancio 1, Francisco A. Rodrigues 1, Luciano da F. Costa 2
arxiv-1612-08388.description: Abstract Many real-world systems can be studied in terms of pattern recognition tasks, so that proper use (and understanding) of machine learning methods in practical applications becomes essential. While a myriad of classification methods have been proposed, there is no consensus on which methods are more suitable for a given dataset.

arxiv-2010-04301.title: Non-Attentive Tacotron: Robust and Controllable Neural TTS Synthesis Including Unsupervised Duration Modeling
arxiv-2010-04301.creator: Jonathan Shen, Ye Jia, Mike Chrzanowski, Yu Zhang, Isaac Elias, Heiga Zen, Yonghui Wu
arxiv-2010-04301.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Shen, Ye Jia, Mike Chrzanowski, Yu Zhang, Isaac Elias, Heiga Zen, Yonghui Wu. This paper presents Non-Attentive Tacotron , a neural text-to-speech model based on Tacotron 2, but replacing the attention mechanism with an explicit duration predictor. The proposed model can be trained either with explicit duration labels, or in an unsupervised or semi-supervised manner using a fine-grained variational auto-encoder for when accurate duration labels are unavailable or scarce in the training data.

arxiv-2012-02150.title: A constructive proof of the convergence of Kalantari’s bound on polynomial zeros
arxiv-2012-02150.creator: Matt Hohertz
arxiv-2012-02150.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Matt Hohertz. In his 2006 paper, Jin proves that Kalantari’s bounds on polynomial zeros, indexed by m ≥ 2 m\geq 2 and called L m L_{m} and U m U_{m} respectively, become sharp as m → ∞ m\rightarrow\infty .

arxiv-2012-03658.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Multilevel Best Linear Unbiased Estimators Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2012-03658.creator: Daniel Schaden, Elisabeth Ullmann
arxiv-2012-03658.description: Abstract We study the computational complexity and variance of multilevel best linear unbiased estimators introduced in [D. Schaden and E. Ullmann, SIAM/ASA J. Uncert. Quantif. , (2020)]. We specialize the results in this work to PDE-based models that are parameterized by a discretization quantity, e.g., the finite element mesh size.

arxiv-2102-00756.title: Theory and simulation of AC electroosmotic suppression of acoustic streaming
arxiv-2102-00756.creator: Bjørn G. Winckelmann, Henrik Bruus
arxiv-2102-00756.description: Abstract Acoustic handling of nanoparticles in resonating acoustofluidic devices is often impeded by the presence of acoustic streaming. For micrometer-sized acoustic chambers, this acoustic streaming is typically driven from the fluid-solid interface by viscous shear-stresses generated by the acoustic actuation. AC electroosmosis is another boundary-driven streaming phenomena routinely used in microfluidic devices for handling of particle suspensions in electrolytes.

arxiv-2107-09259.creator: Taoufik Chtioui , Apurba Das and Sami Mabrouk 1. University of Sfax, Faculty of Sciences Sfax, BP 1171, 3038 Sfax, Tunisia2. At first, we construct a new graded Lie algebra whose Maurer-Cartan elements are given by compatible associative structures.

arxiv-2204-04869.title: Evaluation of Automatic Text Summarization using Synthetic Facts
arxiv-2204-04869.creator: Jay Ahn, Foaad Khosmood
arxiv-2204-04869.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Despite some recent advances, automatic text summarization remains unreliable, elusive and of limited actual use in applications. Two main problems with current summarization methods are well known: evaluation and factual consistency. First, the current evaluation metrics are inadequate. They rely on human generated summaries which are wildly inconsistent and subjective.

arxiv-2402-10756.title: Towards Cohesion-Fairness Harmony: Contrastive Regularization in Individual Fair Graph Clustering
arxiv-2402-10756.creator: Siamak Ghodsi, Seyed Amjad Seyedi, Eirini Ntoutsi
arxiv-2402-10756.description: Abstract Conventional fair graph clustering methods face two primary challenges: i) They prioritize balanced clusters at the expense of cluster cohesion by imposing rigid constraints, ii) Existing methods of both individual and group-level fairness in graph partitioning mostly rely on eigen decompositions and thus, generally lack interpretability.

arxiv-2408-02825.title: The Impact of Environment Configurations on the Stability of AI-Enabled Systems
arxiv-2408-02825.creator: Musfiqur Rahman, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Ahmad Abdellatif, Haya Samaana, Emad Shihab
arxiv-2408-02825.description: Abstract . Nowadays, software systems tend to include Artificial Intelligence (AI) components. Changes in the operational environment have been known to negatively impact the stability of AI-enabled software systems by causing unintended changes in behavior. However, how an environment configuration impacts the behavior of such systems has yet to be explored.

arxiv-2410-19761.title: Physical Simulation for Multi-agent Multi-machine Tending
arxiv-2410-19761.creator: Abdalwhab Abdalwhab, Giovanni Beltrame, David St-Onge
arxiv-2410-19761.description: Abstract The manufacturing sector like many other sectors was recently affected by workforce shortages, a problem that automation and robotics can heavily minimize Kugler 2022 . Simultaneously, Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising solution where robots can learn to perform tasks through interaction and feedback from the environment Singh et al. 2022 .

arxiv-2503-22146.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by O. Benhaida, E. H. Saidi, L. B. Drissi. Haldane’s tight-binding model, which describes a Chern insulator in a two-dimensional hexagonal lattice, exhibits quantum Hall conductivity without an external magnetic field. Here, we explore an α − T 3 \alpha-T_{3} lattice subjected to circularly polarized off-resonance light.

arxiv-2505-14228.description: Abstract . We provide conditional and unconditional asymptotic formulae for the exponential sums ∑ γ γ − i ​ τ \sum_{\gamma}\,\gamma^{-i\tau} , where the summation is over the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros ρ = β + i ​ γ \rho=\beta+i\gamma of the Riemann zeta-function.

arxiv-2508-02271.title: Dynaword: From One-shot to Continuously Developed Datasets
arxiv-2508-02271.creator: Kenneth Enevoldsen, Kristian Nørgaard Jensen, Jan Kostkan, Balázs Szabó, Márton Kardos, Kirsten Vad, Johan Heinsen, Andrea Blasi Núñez, Gianluca Barmina, Jacob Nielsen, Rasmus Larsen, Peter Vahlstrup, Per Møldrup Dalum, Desmond Elliott, Lukas Galke, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Kristoffer Nielbo
arxiv-2508-02271.description: Abstract Large-scale datasets are foundational for research and development in natural language processing. However, current approaches face three key challenges: (1) reliance on ambiguously licensed sources restricting use, sharing, and derivative works; (2) static dataset releases that prevent community contributions and diminish longevity; and (3) quality assurance processes restricted to publishing teams rather than leveraging community expertise.

arxiv-2509-12464.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Accurately Pruned via Chain-of-Thought Reconstruction
arxiv-2509-12464.creator: Ryan Lucas, Kayhan Behdin, Zhipeng Wang, Shao Tang, Qingquan Song, Rahul Mazumder
arxiv-2509-12464.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ryan Lucas, Kayhan Behdin, Zhipeng Wang, Shao Tang, Qingquan Song, Rahul Mazumder. Reasoning language models such as DeepSeek-R1 produce long chain-of-thought traces during inference time which make them costly to deploy at scale. We show that using compression techniques such as neural network pruning produces greater performance loss than in typical language modeling tasks, and in some cases can make the model slower since they cause the model to produce more thinking tokens but with worse performance.

arxiv-2510-06665.title: Doping of a Borexino-like Liquid Scintillator with Tellurium-Diols
arxiv-2510-06665.creator: and Michael Wurm
arxiv-2510-06665.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by and Michael Wurm. One of the most promising approaches for future neutrinoless double beta decay ( 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta ) searches is to incorporate a candidate isotope into the liquid scintillator of a next-generation neutrino detector. In this study, a sample of the high-performance 1,2,4-Trimethylbenzene-based liquid scintillator from the Borexino detector was loaded with different concentrations of Te-diols. Therefore, a novel and completely water-free synthesis in a non-acidic organic environment at room temperature was used.

pmc-10573039.title: Iron Oxide Nanoparticles with Supramolecular Ureido-Pyrimidinone Coating for Antimicrobial Peptide Delivery
pmc-10573039.creator: Chiara Turrina, Jennifer Cookman, Riccardo Bellan, Jiankang Song, Margret Paar, Patricia Y W Dankers, Sonja Berensmeier, Sebastian P Schwaminger, Yuri Lyubchenko
pmc-10573039.description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) can kill bacteria by disrupting their cytoplasmic membrane, which reduces the tendency of antibacterial resistance compared to conventional antibiotics. Their possible toxicity to human cells, however, limits their applicability. The combination of magnetically controlled drug delivery and supramolecular engineering can help to reduce the dosage of AMPs, control the delivery, and improve their cytocompatibility.

pmc-10611269.title: Evaluating the Use of a Robot in a Hematological Intensive Care Unit: A Pilot Study
pmc-10611269.creator: Michela Falcone, Grazia D’Onofrio, Giuseppina Iannacone, Matteo Steduto, Angelo Michele Carella, Francesco Giuliani, Francesco Ricciardi, Iulian I Iordachita
pmc-10611269.description: The aim of the SYRIACA project was to test the capability of a social robot to perform specific tasks in healthcare settings, reducing infection risks for patients and caregivers. The robot was piloted in an Intensive Hematological Unit, where the patients’ and healthcare operators’ acceptability of the robot was evaluated.

pmc-11516109.title: iSECRETE: Integrating Microfluidics and DNA Proximity Amplification for Synchronous Single‐Cell Activation and IFN‐γ Secretion Profiling
pmc-11516109.creator: Ri Lu, Yan Shan Ang, Ka‐Wai Cheung, Kai Yun Quek, Wei‐Xiang Sin, Elizabeth Lee, Shir Lynn Lim, Lin‐Yue Lanry Yung, Michael E Birnbaum, Jongyoon Han, Lih Feng Cheow, Kerwin Kwek Zeming
pmc-11516109.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cytokines, crucial in immune modulation, impact disease progression when their secretion is dysregulated. Existing methods for profiling cytokine secretion suffer from time‐consuming and labor‐intensive processes and often fail to capture the dynamic nature of immune responses. Here, iSECRETE, an integrated platform that enables synchronous cell activation, wash‐free, and target‐responsive protein detection for single‐cell IFN‐γ cytokine secretion analysis within 30 min at room temperature is presented.

pmc-12618512.title: Benchmarking YOLOv8 to YOLOv13 for robust hand gesture recognition in human–robot interaction
pmc-12618512.creator: Yifang Gao, Wei Luo, Shunshun Zhang, Nur Syazreen Ahmad, Xiaojun Wang, Patrick Goh
pmc-12618512.description: Real-time and accurate hand gesture detection is essential for safe and intuitive Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), enabling robots to interpret non-verbal cues and respond appropriately in dynamic environments. This research evaluates the effectiveness of YOLOv8n through YOLOv13n models in recognizing static hand gestures from the TSL detection dataset, which includes 5469 grayscale images across 31 gesture classes.

pmc-13349361.title: Revolutionizing Drug Delivery: The Power of Ultrasound in Ameliorative Effects of Functionalized Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Encapsulated Dacarbazine in a Murine B16F10 Melanoma Model

In this study, we examined the ameliorative effect of ultrasound waves in combination with Functionalized Carbon nanotubes -encapsulated Dacarbazine (fSWCNT-DTIC) in a murine B16F10 melanoma model.Materials and Methods:The Preparation of single-walled carbon nanotube encapsulated Dacarbazine (fSWCNT-DTIC) accrued at several steps.

pmc-13352282.creator: Kyle Wm. Hall, Timothy W. Sirk, Wataru Shinoda, Michael L. Klein, K. Michael Salerno
pmc-13352282.description: This work examines the response of semicrystalline polyethylene under triaxial strain. The Shinoda-DeVane-Klein (SDK) model of polyethylene (PE) was used in coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of more than 2 × 106 particles, representing more than 2 × 107 atoms and a volume of greater than 105 nm3. pmc-13380098.title: Extending the global landscape of Bruck syndrome: Case series of Indonesian and Ukrainian patients with PLOD2 pathogenic variants and literature review
pmc-13380098.creator: Devina Afraditya Paveta, Agustini Utari, Ferdy Kurniawan Cayami, Alessandra Maugeri, Aare Märtson, Sulev Kõks, Andrii Pashenko, Sergii Khmyzov, Elisabeth Marelise W Eekhoff, Katre Maasalu, Dimitra Micha, Lidiia Zhytnik
pmc-13380098.description: Bruck syndrome type 2 (BRKS2) is a rare disorder marked by congenital joint contractures and bone fragility, caused by variants in PLOD2, which encodes lysyl hydroxylase 2 essential for collagen stability. We report the first genetically confirmed BRKS2 cases from Indonesia and Ukraine, both showing fractures, skeletal deformities, and contractures.

pmc-13442310.title: A Covalent Organic Framework With Staggered Topology for Mimetic Transmembrane Transport of Hydrated Ions
pmc-13442310.creator: Xuan Li, Jiaxin Liu, Yilin Zhang, Zhixiang Dai, Zihan Tan, Hongli Yang, Chao Xu, Shengyang Zhou, Zhong‐Ming Li
pmc-13442310.description: In biological systems, hydrated‐ions cross protein channels with exceptional high efficiency through a structural dehydration‐compensation mechanism, where protein conformational adjustments contract the channel and enable electron‐rich sites to coordinate with ions, offsetting their dehydration energy without external energy input. In this work, we discovered that a typical β‐ketoenamine‐linked covalent organic framework (COF) with staggered‐stacking architectures exhibits a similar mechanism.
